Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, head of US European Command, has privately warned the Pentagon that he lacks enough naval assets to keep intercepting Iranian ballistic missiles aimed at Israel while also covering the US homeland — and is requesting an additional Navy destroyer to avoid having to choose between the two, according to a Washington Post report citing anonymous officials.

Grynkewich's forces currently rely on destroyers based in Rota, Spain — five deployed, with a sixth expected later this year — that rotate through the eastern Mediterranean and Red Sea to shoot down Iranian and Ansar Allah projectiles headed for Israel. As of Friday, only two of those destroyers were stationed in the Mediterranean.

EUCOM is also responsible for NATO's eastern flank and countering "Russian long-range missile threats" — meaning the same limited destroyer fleet is being pulled in multiple directions by months of near-daily intercept operations tied to the Iran war.

The warning comes alongside other reports of strain across the US arsenal, including dwindling Patriot interceptor stocks.
